Smith, John Phone: 98623487 email: heathermorris@example.net Date of Birth: 1987-03-10
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the effectiveness of treatment for generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, as well as to address any new symptoms or concerns since the last visit.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment today, reporting both positive and negative developments since his last visit. He states that his anxiety levels have improved slightly, attributing this change to the continuation of sertraline at 300 mg daily and the introduction of cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), which he began two weeks ago. He expresses optimism about the therapy but notes that situational anxiety remains a challenge, particularly during high-pressure meetings at work.
Regarding his insomnia, Mr. Smith reports that trazodone at 100 mg at bedtime has been effective in helping him fall asleep; however, he continues to experience nocturnal awakenings, averaging twice per night. He has increased his melatonin dosage to 10 mg, which he feels has contributed to a marginal improvement in sleep quality, although he still wakes feeling somewhat fatigued.
His tension-type headaches have persisted, now occurring three times weekly. He describes the intensity as moderate to severe, with some episodes rated at 8 out of 10 on the pain scale. While ibuprofen 600 mg provides temporary relief, he is interested in exploring preventive measures. He has been diligent with topiramate at 150 mg daily but expresses concern over the frequency of his headaches.
Mr. Smith continues to report persistent fatigue, which he attributes to ongoing work-related stress and anxiety. Although bupropion at 150 mg daily has helped some, he feels that his energy levels fluctuate significantly throughout the day.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 100 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 4. Ibuprofen 600 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 5. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (discontinued due to sedation and lack of efficacy) 6. Topiramate 150 mg daily (continued) 7. Lorazepam 1 mg twice daily as needed (continued) 8. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime (increased for improved sleep quality) 9. Modafinil 100 mg in the morning (continued) 10. Bupropion 150 mg daily (continued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to adhere to a healthy lifestyle, maintaining a balanced diet and regular exercise regimen, including yoga and brisk walking. He reports that while he has reduced caffeine intake, work stress occasionally interferes with his ability to engage in mindfulness practices.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety is somewhat better managed with CBT; sleep quality remains a concern; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency increased; intensity remains moderate to severe; no dizziness or visual disturbances noted. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue continues, with some fluctuations; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 118/76 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented; appears mildly fatigued but engaged; mood appears stable with moderate anxiety. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no tenderness in the temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with moderate anxiety.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Continue CBT sessions; evaluate progress at the next visit. Lorazepam at 1 mg twice daily as needed for acute anxiety will remain on the regimen. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 100 mg at bedtime. Monitor melatonin effects; consider further adjustments if sleep quality does not improve in the next month. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 150 mg daily; maintain ibuprofen at 600 mg as needed. If headache frequency or intensity does not improve, a referral to a neurologist will be warranted to explore additional preventive therapies. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Continue bupropion at 150 mg daily; emphasize the importance of regular exercise and stress management. Re-evaluate fatigue levels and consider additional interventions if there is no improvement by the next appointment.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-05-01 to monitor symptom progression, medication efficacy, and any new concerns. Mr. Smith is advised to maintain a detailed log of his symptoms, medication responses, and any triggers for his anxiety or headaches to facilitate ongoing management.
